note: Single source of truth for hardware values. Edit this file, then run tools/gen_device_spec.py; do not hand-edit the generated header or Python module. Every numeric group names one source id from the sources table below.

model.cb_depth_basis: tt-metal reader/compute/writer examples start at two tiles per circular buffer; the allocator clamps the request to the L1 budget.
model.l1_reserve_basis: Planner reserve for kernel code, stack, and runtime bookkeeping. This is a project planning choice, not a vendor figure.
model.fidelity_phases_basis: The project models one fidelity phase for the bf16 matmul path; the matrix unit needs one instruction per phase.

sources.supports: Wormhole card specifications: 80 Tensix on the die, n150 72 Tensix at 1 GHz with 12 GB GDDR6 at 288 GB/s and 160 W, n300 two ASICs with 64 Tensix each and 24 GB at 576 GB/s and 300 W, PCIe 4.0 x16, 2x QSFP-DD 200G, Ubuntu 22.04
Blackhole card specifications: 120 Tensix, up to 1.35 GHz, p100a 28 GB GDDR6 at 448 GB/s, p150a 32 GB at 512 GB/s, 300 W, PCIe 5.0 x16, p150a 4x QSFP-DD 800G, 180 MB SRAM, Ubuntu 22.04
Wormhole physical description: 10x12 NoC coordinate grid, 80 functional Tensix workers, arch name WORMHOLE_B0, worker L1 size 1499136 bytes
Wormhole compute grids and dispatch: nebula_x1 row dispatch compute grid 8x8 for n150, nebula_x2 row dispatch compute grid 8x7 for n300
Blackhole physical description: 17x12 NoC coordinate grid, 140 functional Tensix workers, arch name BLACKHOLE, worker L1 size 1572864 bytes
Blackhole compute grids and column dispatch: unharvested 13x10, 1x harvested 12x10, 2x harvested 11x10
L1 size per Tensix tile: 1464 KiB on Wormhole and 1536 KiB on Blackhole; each NoC can read 256 bits per cycle and write 256 bits per cycle against L1
Matrix unit throughput: 4.096 TFLOP/s per core at 1 GHz and one fidelity phase, one to four fidelity phases, and 72/64/80 Tensix tiles per n150/n300/Galaxy part
NoC structure: two physically separate NoCs, 256-bit flits (32 bytes), and packets of one header flit plus up to 256 data flits (8192 data bytes)
Toolchain minimums: Ubuntu 22.04, tt-kmd v2.8.0 or above, firmware v19.8.1, tt-smi v5.0.0 or above, IOMMU required

notes: The die has 80 Tensix workers on a 10x8 subset of the 10x12 NoC coordinate grid; the product harvests one row for 72 workers, and tt-metal reserves the last row for dispatch, leaving the 8x8 compute grid.
SRAM is the product-page aggregate of 108 MB counted as 1.5 MiB per Tensix tile; usable per-core L1 is 1499136 bytes.
The vendor page states 12 GB of GDDR6; this file records the capacity as 12 GiB bytes to match the project fact sheet.
The matrix unit figures hold for Wormhole at 1 GHz and one fidelity phase; the n150 TeraFLOPS ratings on the product page assume the same matrix unit.
Two Wormhole ASICs per board; each die harvests two rows for 64 Tensix workers, and tt-metal reserves the last row for dispatch, leaving an 8x7 compute grid per chip.
The 576 GB/s DRAM bandwidth and 24 GiB capacity are board aggregates across the two ASICs; the bandwidth row in this file is the aggregate the board reports.
SRAM is the product-page aggregate of 192 MB counted as 1.5 MiB per Tensix tile over 128 tiles.
The vendor page states 24 GB of GDDR6; this file records the capacity as 24 GiB bytes to match the project fact sheet.

Three Blackhole core counts disagree and this file does not pick one silently: the soc descriptor lists 140 functional Tensix workers on the die, the unharvested core descriptor lists a 13x10 compute grid (130), and the product page lists 120 Tensix cores. The scheduler models the product figure: the 1x harvested descriptor grid of 12x10 equals 120.
The die has 17x12 NoC coordinates; the Tensix workers occupy 14 columns by 10 rows.
SRAM is the product-page aggregate of 180 MB counted as 1.5 MiB per Tensix tile over 120 product cores.
The vendor page states 28 GB of GDDR6; this file records the capacity as 28 GiB bytes to match the project fact sheet.
The 4096 FLOPs per cycle per core figure comes from the matrix unit; at 1.35 GHz across 120 cores the same figure reproduces the product page BLOCKFP8 rating of 664 TFLOP/s.
The NoC block uses the Wormhole ISA documentation because the retrieved Blackhole ISA set has no NoC page; tt-metal configures noc0 and noc1 on Blackhole.
